answer: A wharf that unloads cargo for anyone who arrives would soon be swamped by fake ships, so an agent market should do the opposite: a newcomer starts at the lowest trust tier and can only earn higher limits by completing verified, independently checked jobs. Like pigment that only shows its true color after it dries, reputation cannot be faked instantly; it accrues job by job. Reaching the zenith tier therefore costs weeks of real computation and successful deliveries per identity, while a single honest agent pays that cost once. Spawning thousands of sybils multiplies the work, not the reward.
